item: V-lane: uvx/PyPI version-freshness audit of MCP servers (registry C:/Users/Prekzursil/.agents/agents.json + live ~/.claude.json), 2026-09-19. 10 PyPI packages double-mechanism verified (PyPI JSON API + pip index versions, full agreement), plus uv-cache third signal. Read-only; no config writes, no commits, no server spawns.

steps.detail: Filtered agents.json mcp.servers (92 servers) for uvx/uv/PyPI commands: 7 uvx servers (arxiv, crossref, docker, excel, pubmed-tool, scrapegraph, tooluniverse). Same filter on live ~/.claude.json mcpServers (87 entries) added 3 ungoverned uvx extras (elevenlabs, mcp-windbg, serena) plus 1 venv-based PyPI install (paper-search). Other .venv servers (angr, frida, mitmproxy, apktool, jadx, ocr, rdkit, schrodinger...) are local git/source installs with no PyPI registry pin - out of V-lane scope.

Pin quoted in config: 'tooluniverse==1.2.4'. PyPI latest 1.5.0 (pip index agrees; releases show 1.2.4, 1.2.6, 1.3.0, 1.3.1, 1.4.0, 1.4.1, 1.5.0 above the pin; 1.2.5 absent from the list). Drift: 3 minor releases behind. Cache D:/uv/cache/wheels-v6/pypi/tooluniverse holds BOTH 1.2.4 and 1.3.0 - a second consumer resolved 1.3.0 at some point (origin UNVERIFIED; .codex/config.toml has no mcp_servers entry, only a plugins line 714 'tooluniverse@claude-cowork' - settling experiment: grep McpHub/plugin launch configs for uvx tooluniverse). Also: server reported CONNECTION_CLOSED at this session start (axis D lane).
steps.risk: MINOR drift (1.2.4 -> 1.5.0); pinned, so drift is deliberate-but-stale; upgrade = bump pin, forces uv re-resolve + env rebuild on next spawn

steps.detail: Pin: 'scrapegraph-mcp==1.0.1'. PyPI latest 1.0.1 (only releases: 1.0.1, 1.0.0). Cache holds exactly 1.0.1. Zero drift.

Floating pin 'uvx arxiv-mcp-server' (no version constraint). PyPI latest 0.7.2; cache holds 0.7.2 -> floating resolution is currently at latest. Un-pinned means the next re-resolve can silently pick up a new 0.x minor (breaking-change-prone range).
steps.risk: no current drift; floating = latent uncontrolled upgrade

steps.detail: Floating pin with dependency overlay '--with mcp<2 crossref-mcp'. PyPI latest 0.1.0 and it is the ONLY release ever published; cache holds 0.1.0. The mcp<2 constraint is the deliberate compat shim recorded in the 2026-09-21 wiring receipt (uvx --with 'mcp<2' crossref-mcp) - keep it on any version bump.
steps.risk: no drift possible yet (single upstream release); config-quality: dep overlay is intentional, not cruft

steps.detail: Floating pin 'uvx.exe docker-mcp'. PyPI latest 0.2.0 (releases 0.2.0, 0.1.0); cache holds 0.2.0 -> currently at latest.
Floating pin 'uvx.exe excel-mcp-server stdio'. PyPI latest 0.1.8; cache holds 0.1.8 -> at latest.
Floating pin via --from. PyPI latest 0.1.0 (only release); cache holds 0.1.0. Server reported CONNECTION_CLOSED at this session start (axis D lane; wheels are cached so not a download failure).
steps.risk: no drift possible yet (single release); floating

steps.detail: Ungoverned extra (in ~/.claude.json only, absent from registry). Pin 0.15.0; PyPI latest 1.3.0 (pip index agrees; releases run 0.15.0 -> 1.0.0 -> 1.3.0). Cache holds 0.15.0 AND 1.2.2 - second consumer evidence, origin UNVERIFIED. Biggest drift in lane; 1.x line adds features (transport flag already used here suggests someone tracked upstream once).
steps.risk: MAJOR drift (0.15.0 -> 1.3.0); also governance gap: ungoverned surface

steps.detail: Ungoverned extra. Floating 'uvx elevenlabs-mcp'; PyPI latest 0.12.2; cache holds 0.9.1, 0.10.0, 0.11.0, 0.12.2 - direct evidence that floating uvx pins DO advance to PyPI latest over successive resolutions (not frozen forever). Currently at latest.
steps.risk: no current drift; floating; ungoverned surface

steps.detail: Ungoverned extra pinned to a git URL, not PyPI - drift axis is upstream HEAD, unbounded and un-auditable against registries. Settling experiment for anyone adopting: pin a commit hash.
steps.risk: unbounded drift (implicit @HEAD); no registry pin exists

steps.detail: Not uvx: direct venv exe. Installed version read from dist-info on disk: paper_search_mcp-0.1.4 == PyPI latest 0.1.4 (releases 0.1.0-0.1.4). Zero drift. Unlike uvx servers, upgrades here require explicit pip install -U in that venv.

uv 0.10.4 (079e3fd05 2026-02-17), cache at D:/uv/cache (wheels-v6, environments-v2, sdists-v9, simple-v20). (1) A pin bump (e.g. tooluniverse 1.2.4->1.5.0) forces uv to fetch the new wheel, rebuild the ephemeral env, and re-lock on the NEXT spawn - first spawn is slower and requires network; stale 1.2.4 entries linger until 'uv cache prune'. (2) Floating pins are not frozen: elevenlabs cache lineage 0.9.1->0.12.2 proves re-resolution advances them to latest; exact re-resolve trigger policy (env-hash miss vs TTL) UNVERIFIED - settling experiment: 'uv tool run --help' / uv docs caching page, or a controlled offline spawn after cache clean in a sandbox. (3) Exact trigger for the historical 1.3.0/1.2.2 out-of-pin resolutions UNVERIFIED (see tooluniverse step).
steps.risk: operational: post-bump first-spawn latency + offline failure window on any uvx server whose env needs (re)building

steps.action: config-quality notes (axis C, incidental to V-lane)
steps.detail: (1) glm53-space uses 'uv run --locked --directory ...' (lockfile-enforced) while qdx-rush uses 'uv run --directory ...' WITHOUT --locked - qdx-rush deps float per uv resolution on spawn; consider --locked for parity. (2) Floating pins on young 0.x packages (arxiv, docker, excel, pubmed-tool, elevenlabs) are the main freshness/fragility trade: pinning gives reproducibility at the cost of manual bumps; current estate pattern works only because re-resolution happens to track latest. (3) mcp-windbg + elevenlabs + serena are ungoverned live extras - V-lane confirms they are also the drift/governance outliers.
